hops.input: Read-only focused code review. User asks Forge Kirby to look like the existing main Pink friend. Full relevant source files and old published-code fixture provided, no secrets/student data. New createRecipe Kirby uses appearance="welcome-v1"; legacy recipes omit marker, retain old generic body/code verbatim. New model reads main welcomeParts Kirby, scales body/limbs, surface tangent frames for layered eyes, copies mouth/tongue and main colors, shininess .28 = main roughness .72. Hex colors are converted sRGB->linear only for new appearance and both preview and generated Python use same converter. New preview camera/light matches main base lighting. Existing posted code must still pass moduleFromPublishedCode equality. Only untouched unnamed starter drafts refresh; edited/named/saved/forked drafts must survive. Tests compare each main part transform/material and real CPython export, retain old fixture bytes and slider extrema. Do not execute/edit/call other agents. Identify concrete remaining P1/P2 only (metadata/code equality, float/sign, standard VPython axes, draft data loss); otherwise say none. Cite file:line. Under 4500 characters. No broad redesign.
hops.output:
**Verdict: not ready. There is one definite P1 and three P2s. I read the code only and ran nothing. `engine/vpython-bridge`, `test/python-runner`, `forge/registry` and the server code aren't in the snapshot.**

## P1

**1. `forgeColorVector` is used in `modules.js` but never imported.**
- `client__src__forge__modules.js:51` calls it, but the import at `modules.js:1` doesn't include it, and it's only defined and exported at `recipes.js:76`.
- Every `moduleDefinition` call throws `ReferenceError`, for all presets, not just Kirby. That covers `Forge.jsx:29`, which runs on render, so the Forge page crashes.
- `moduleFromPublishedCode` catches the error at `modules.js:26` and returns `null`, so **every existing published module fails the equality check**.
- Fix: add it to the import on line 1. If this snapshot is what was tested, the reported test results can't be from this code, so rerun them after the fix.

## P2

**2. Two checks in the main parity test fail regardless of the geometry.**
- **Part names:** `recipes.js:87` rewrites `-` to `minus`, so the IDs are `forge_eye_minus1`, `forge_cheek_minus1` and so on. `kirby.test.js:23` looks up the raw `eye_-1`, gets `undefined`, and throws at `.props`. `kirby.test.js:17` has the same mismatch through `getMesh`. Normalize with `part.name.replaceAll('-','minus')`.
- **Colour comparison:** `kirby.test.js:20` uses exact `toEqual` against `THREE.Color`. As I recall, Three's sRGB conversion uses truncated constants (`c*0.0773993808`, `c*0.9478672986+0.0521327014`), while `recipes.js:76` uses `/12.92` and `/1.055`. If so, the last bits differ. Use `toBeCloseTo`, as line 51 already does.

**3. Non-unit-size parts emit `axis` with a magnitude that doesn't match `size.x`.**
- Eyes get `axis=left_eye_axis * scale` (unit length, `recipes.js:106,112,124`, `modules.js:75`). The right hand gets the same at `recipes.js:132`. Meanwhile `size.x` is .255, .17, .115 or .43.
- In VPython, axis magnitude and `size.x` are coupled. This repo already treats them that way: `welcome-friends.js:143,178` writes `axis = ... * size.x`.
- I couldn't check the real `vpython` constructor order here, so I don't know which value wins when both are passed. If axis wins, the copied or GitHub `.py` gets eyes and a hand about 2–9x too wide, and any later `size`/`axis` change would behave inconsistently.
- `welcomeDefinition` has the same pattern (`welcome-friends.js:91-97`), so matching main doesn't prove this is safe.
- The export test wouldn't catch it. `kirby.test.js:49-51` checks only position and colour, not size or orientation, so the "real CPython export" claim doesn't cover transforms. It also needs confirming whether `python-runner` uses real `vpython` or a shim.
- Fix: emit `axis` as unit × `size.x`, in both the code and the value, and assert size and quaternion on the export path.

**4. `cheek_size = 0` now creates zero-size parts.**
- The slider minimum is 0 (`recipes.js:28`). The legacy path skips cheeks at or below .005 (`recipes.js:157`).
- The new path always emits them with `size=(0,0,0)` (`recipes.js:103,126`), which gives a singular scale and a zero axis inside `compound`. Standard VPython behaviour here is unverified.
- The extrema test only checks that the run didn't error. Skip cheeks with the same guard in the welcome loop.

## Must verify (outside the snapshot)

- **Publish round trip:** `Forge.jsx:59` rebuilds from `result.recipe`. If the server or registry whitelists recipe keys and drops `appearance`, a new Kirby silently becomes legacy: the header and code change, with welcome parameters on the old body. Confirm the server keeps `appearance`, and that any server copy of `recipes.js` can resolve `../data/welcome-friends.js` (`recipes.js:1`).

## Checked, no issue found

- **Legacy bytes and hash:** `delete recipe.appearance` (`recipes.js:48`) restores the old key order, so `make_kirby_62f62faf` and the header stay stable. Range, center and forward all stay on the legacy branch.
- **New-recipe equality:** key order matches between `createRecipe` and `validateRecipe`, with `appearance` last, so the header round-trips and the hash is stable. `appearance` is rejected on non-Kirby recipes and for unknown values.
- **Eye frame signs:**
  - The normal is the correct ellipsoid gradient.
  - `axis` and `cross(normal, axis)` match `welcome-friends.js:28-29` algebraically.
  - The right hand's (cos, sin) axis and (−sin, cos) up equal `rotateZ(-.6)`.
  - `center` correctly removes the .018 normal offset.
  - `String(Number(toFixed(6)))` can't emit `-0` or exponent notation.
- **Slider ranges:** preset defaults are within range, and `front()` stays above the `.05` clamp at the gap extrema.
- **Camera:** `scene.forward` and the preview camera offset agree in sign (`modules.js:110`, `ForgePreview.jsx:61`).
- **Draft loss:** I found no path that loses a draft. The refresh guard rejects a saved ID, `appearance`, `recordId`, `source`, references, description, title, expression, accessory, colours and any parameter change, and it keeps `id` and metadata. The login-transfer path passes `modules` that include `saved.draft`.

## Non-blocking

- The linear colours match VPyLab's bridge, but real VPython/GlowScript likely writes colour vectors straight to the display. The downloaded `.py` may look darker than main there. Treat this as a known tradeoff, or note it in the export copy.
